```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The post-treatment order q is a maintained structural choice. Validation of a
pre-treatment predictive q does not establish the causal continuation law.
R is a root-energy sensitivity radius and is not learned from kappa.

```{r}
library(TRSC)
g <- trsc_geometry(matrix(c(0, 1), 1, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B"))))
X <- matrix(rep(c(0, 1), 3), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE,
            dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "B")))
level <- c(A = .6, B = .4)
previous <- c(A = .7, B = .3)
persistent <- trsc_counterfactual_set(g, X, level, q = 1, R = 0)
affine <- trsc_counterfactual_set(g, X, level, q = 2, R = 0, previous = previous)
trsc_bounds(persistent)
trsc_bounds(affine)
```

q=1 centers at 0.4; q=2 centers at 0.5, 0.6, 0.7. This example has
evaluation-invariant profiles; generally fixed profiles still permit fibers.

## Affine continuation can leave the hull

```{r}
minimum <- trsc_min_radius(g, c(A = 0, B = 1), q = 2, H = 2,
                          previous = c(A = 1, B = 0))
minimum[c("lower", "upper", "estimate", "status")]
boundary <- trsc_counterfactual_set(g, X[1:2, ], c(A = 0, B = 1),
                                  q = 2, R = 1, previous = c(A = 1, B = 0))
trsc_sensitivity(boundary, c(.5, 1, 1.1, 2), a = c(1, -1))
```

The minimum root curvature is 1. Certified infeasibility is an explicit status,
not an NA result. Close to the numerical minimum, inspect both certified
minimum-radius bounds and solver status. A solver candidate alone cannot
settle feasibility. Support enclosures can become less sharp when the solver
does not supply a useful dual.

For inference, q=1 has level uncertainty; q=2 also carries slope uncertainty,
whose affine-center contribution grows with horizon. Hull constraints may
truncate it. This is an informational burden, not a rule for preferring q=1.
